summary: Place authored marks where they explain shape, use or attention rather than covering every surface with equal detail.
objective: Brush marks stay attached to the intended part, seams are unobtrusive, and detail survives the normal viewing distance.
example_prompts: Create a hand-painted market stall with brushwork following each timber and cloth panel.

principles: Place authored marks where they explain shape, use or attention rather than covering every surface with equal detail.
implementation: Model the silhouette and major relief; assign surface regions so brushwork can follow boards, cloth or panels.
Paint selected gradients, edge accents and variation; keep illumination choices deliberate so painted highlights do not fight the scene light.
Use close and mid-distance views to set mark scale; move the camera around a static object before approving animated lighting.
Author at 512 px/m texel density on hero props and 256 px/m on background, and keep painted marks 8-20 px wide at that density so they survive a 2 m viewing distance.
Paint three values per material region (base, occlusion at 0.7x, edge light at 1.3x), hold hue jitter within +/-8 degrees, and leave about 40% of each surface unmarked so the marks read as intent.
observable_checks: Brush marks stay attached to the intended part, seams are unobtrusive, and detail survives the normal viewing distance.

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at renderer.toneMappingExposure 1.0; re-tune intensities and fog density under a different tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with stylized or low-poly forms; painted appearance is not evidence of historical fabrication or measured material behavior.

defaults.rationale: Here the painting, not the rig, owns the value structure, so the key:fill ratio is flattened to 2:1 and the light colours are kept under 20% saturation - a strong directional rig would re-shade surfaces that already contain painted occlusion and edge light. Roughness stays high (0.7-0.95) with no normal maps so no specular competes with the painted highlights.

values.value_structure: 35/45/20 dark/mid/light; the darks come from painted occlusion, not from the light rig
values.saturation_rule: painted texture carries the saturation (accent up to 70%); scene light colours stay under 20% saturation so they do not double-tint the art

lights.ratio: key:fill ~ 2:1 - deliberately flat so the painted values are not overwritten

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: roughness read from the painted map (0.7 varnished, 0.95 raw timber); no normal maps - relief lives in the diffuse painting

values.signature_technique: occlusion and edge light painted into the diffuse map, then lit at a flat 2:1 ratio so the painting remains the dominant value structure
never: uniform noise texture over every surface
specular strong enough to compete with painted highlights
a visible tiling seam across a focal part
